\chapter{Boolean Analysis --- Holder}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.Cube.Reverse.Holder
\section{Overview}
Reverse Young and reverse Hölder inequalities bound pairings of nonnegative cube functions from below. The negative conjugate exponent uses the extended power-mean convention at zeros.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{lemma}[Reverse Young inequality]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.reverse_young}
\leanok
\difficulty{5}
Let $0<r<1$, $a\ge0$, and $b>0$. Writing $s=r/(r-1)<0$, one has $ab\ge a^r/r+b^s/s$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Positivity of a nonnegative moment]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.ReverseMoments.expect_rpow_pos}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.uniformWeight}
\difficulty{4}
Let $r\in\bbr$ and $u:\{0,1\}^n\to[0,\infty)$ have at least one positive value. Then $\E[u^r]>0$, with the convention $0^0=1$ and $0^r=0$ for $r\ne0$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Normalizing a power moment]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.ReverseMoments.expect_normalized_rpow_eq_one}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.expect}
\difficulty{3}
Let $r\ne0$, let $u:\{0,1\}^n\to[0,\infty)$, and assume $A=\E[u^r]>0$ under the uniform measure. Then $\E[(u/A^{1/r})^r]=1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Rescaling a pairing]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.innerProduct_eq_mul_expect_div}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct}
\difficulty{3}
Let $u,v:\{0,1\}^n\to\bbr$ and nonzero $A,B\in\bbr$, uniform expectation satisfies $\E[uv]=AB\E[(u/A)(v/B)]$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Reverse Holder with a positive exponent]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.reverse_holder_of_pos}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.IsNonnegative, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.ReverseMoments.expect_normalized_rpow_eq_one, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.ReverseMoments.expect_rpow_pos, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.innerProduct_eq_mul_expect_div, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.lpMean, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.lpMean_of_pos, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.reverse_young, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.expect_eq_fintypeExpect, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct, BooleanAnalysis.uniformWeight}
\difficulty{5}
Let $0<r<1$ and $u,v:\{0,1\}^n\to[0,\infty)$. Then $\E[uv]\ge M_r(u)M_{r/(r-1)}(v)$. For nonnegative functions $u$, the extended mean is $M_r(u)=(\E u^r)^{1/r}$ when $r>0$; the same formula applies for $r<0$ when $u$ is positive everywhere. For positive $u$, $M_0(u)=\exp(\E\log u)$; if $r\le0$ and $u$ has a zero, $M_r(u)=0$. All expectations are uniform.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Reverse Holder for finite conjugate exponents]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.reverse_holder}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.IsNonnegative, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.lpMean, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.reverse_holder_of_pos, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct_comm}
\difficulty{4}
Let $p<1$, $p\ne0$, and $f,g:\{0,1\}^n\to[0,\infty)$. Then $\E[fg]\ge M_p(f)M_{p/(p-1)}(g)$. For nonnegative functions $u$, the extended mean is $M_r(u)=(\E u^r)^{1/r}$ when $r>0$; the same formula applies for $r<0$ when $u$ is positive everywhere. For positive $u$, $M_0(u)=\exp(\E\log u)$; if $r\le0$ and $u$ has a zero, $M_r(u)=0$. All expectations are uniform.
\end{lemma}
